key_insight: CORTEX adds structured, stage-by-stage reasoning traces to 3D chest CT questions so MLLMs can explain answers in a way that is easier to interpret and verify.
clinical_relevance: This could improve trustworthiness of chest CT AI by making model reasoning more aligned with radiology workflow and clinician review.
method: Built a benchmark on CT-RATE for open-ended VQA, closed-ended VQA, and report generation.
Created four-stage diagnostic traces: task understanding, visual observation, diagnostic reasoning, and answer synthesis.
Used automated rubric scoring plus expert radiologist review to filter and validate traces.
evidence_signal: The dataset contains 76,177 validated reasoning traces, with both structured supervision and stage-level evaluation protocols designed with clinicians.
watch_item: The traces are model-generated and filtered, so real-world reliability still depends on how well this structured reasoning transfers to diverse scanners, patients, and clinical settings.
paper_title: CORTEX: A Structured Reasoning Benchmark for Trustworthy 3D Chest CT MLLMs
